newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline prices edge up, EU supplies also rise.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline prices edge up, EU supplies also rise.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices edged higher in quiet trading on the back of a rebound in crude oil futures and support near $200 in Eurograde barges, traders said.

But some traders warned that the fundamentals were still bearish -- European Union gasoline supplies rose in the latest month and the arbitrage to the States is closed for smaller 30,000 tonne vessels.

Oil traders did say on Tuesday that some European oil refineries have cut production and others were considering following suit because of poor returns on sales in a weakening late-winter heating oil market.
And British Petroleum said on Tuesday that margins at its refineries in January were "very disappointing," and that some of its business managers were considering cutting crude throughput.
Eurograde barges were heard up $3 at $206/$208 fob ARA, after early offers near $210 found few willing buyers, sources said. Regular unleaded held at a $5 backwardation, trading at $201/$203.
"I don't think we've seen the end of the line yet," for lower gasoline prices, said one trader in Germany, who said local demand was lacklustre.
"We need exports into the Western Hemisphere to get the market back in balance because we're getting long again," he said.
Euroilstock said gasoline inventories in the European Union, excluding Sweden, rose 8.16 million barrels in January to 164.60 million.
